headline: HDFC Bank delivered mixed guidance execution in Q3-FY26: contingent provision build of Rs.1,600 crores was met precisely, NIM tailwind from deposit repricing is materialising (10-11 bps cost-of-funds reduction in the quarter) but full margin recovery remains incomplete, and loan growth at 12% YoY improved sharply from 5.5% but fell short of system pace of ~13.5-13.9%, leaving the 'grow in line with system' FY26 target technically unmet. Credit-to-Deposit Ratio glide path and ROA recovery trajectory remain works-in-progress with no definitive resolution this quarter.

segments.Whole Bank: Deposit repricing is flowing through as guided — cost of funds fell 10-11 bps in Q3, confirming the NIM tailwind thesis, though margins remain below pre-merger levels with four to five quarters of repricing still to play out. Loan growth accelerated to 12% YoY (from 5.5%) but lagged system growth of ~13.5-13.9%, meaning the FY26 'grow at market pace' objective was not fully achieved; management reaffirmed confidence in outpacing system growth in FY27. Contingent provisions were built by exactly Rs.1,600 crores as stated, reinforcing balance sheet resilience. CD ratio remains above 90 with management guiding to a 90-96% range for FY26 exit and 85-90% by FY27-end, though Q3 deposit growth decelerated due to deliberate rate discipline on non-retail segments. ROA trajectory was not explicitly quantified in Q3 disclosures, leaving the 1.8-1.95% improvement claim unverified.

keyThemes: NIM recovery pace: four to five quarters of time-deposit repricing tailwind remain; watch cost-of-funds trajectory and any rate-cut impact on asset yields in Q4-FY26 and FY27
Loan growth vs. system: FY27 commitment to grow faster than system requires deposit mobilisation to accelerate materially — granular retail deposit momentum is the critical execution variable

CD ratio glide path credibility: management flagged tactical missteps on non-retail deposit pricing in Q3; Q4 execution on deposit growth will determine whether FY26 exit lands in the guided 90-96% band

Regulatory and one-off risk: Rs.5 billion agri provision absorbed in Q3 with potential recalibration of agri book ahead; labour code provisioning estimate (~Rs.8 billion) carries rule-making uncertainty and could revise materially when final regulations are issued
